question: What is the main goal of diagnostic testing for hormone (endocrine) disorders?

options.B: To permanently replace missing organ functions
options.C: To cure infectious agents causing gland failure
options.D: To measure hormone levels and check organ response

explanation: You've got this! Endocrine tests simply check how much hormone is in the body and see how target organs respond to signals. It is all about checking the balance. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is exact timing so important when collecting blood for hormone tests?

options.A: Hormones break down within seconds after leaving the bloodstream
options.B: Patient fasting has no effect on most endocrine lab results
options.C: Laboratory technicians only process hormone samples in the morning
options.D: Hormone levels change based on daily body rhythms and activities

explanation: Great job thinking like a nurse! Many hormones rise and fall throughout the day or shift with meals, so getting the timing right is key to an accurate result. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h1)

question: What does a 'free hormone' blood test actually measure?

options.A: The rate at which the liver destroys excess hormones
options.B: Only the active hormone not bound to carrier proteins
options.C: Only the inactive hormones attached to transport molecules
options.D: The total amount of protein stored inside the endocrine gland

explanation: Think of free hormones as the ones floating around free and ready to work! Unbound hormones are the active fraction available to affect the body. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why would a doctor order an antibody blood test for someone with a suspected endocrine problem?

options.A: To test how quickly the kidneys filter out waste products
options.B: To determine if the patient has a bacterial infection
options.C: To check for autoimmune destruction of endocrine tissue
options.D: To measure the exact weight and size of the pituitary gland

explanation: Spot on! Antibody tests help us see if the body's immune system is mistakenly attacking its own hormone glands, like in thyroid disorders. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main perk of doing a 24-hour urine collection instead of just one blood test?

options.A: It captures total hormone output and smooths out hourly spikes
options.B: It measures intracellular hormone synthesis inside the bone marrow
options.C: It requires no special patient preparation or storage rules
options.D: It can be completed in less than five minutes at the bedside

explanation: Hormones can spike and dip all day long. Collecting urine over a full 24 hours gives a complete, average picture of what the body is putting out! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h3)

question: How does a 'stimulation test' help us figure out an endocrine issue?

options.A: It forces the pancreas to stop making insulin during high stress
options.B: It tests if an underactive gland can produce hormones when given a trigger
options.C: It measures the permanent destruction of the pituitary stalk
options.D: It permanently blocks all hormone receptors in peripheral tissues

explanation: You're doing great! If a gland is acting lazy, we give it a special trigger (stimulation) to see if it still has the energy to wake up and produce hormones. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main goal of an endocrine suppression test?

options.A: To measure how fast the kidneys reabsorb glucose from the urine
options.B: To see if a gland stops producing hormones when given a suppressing agent
options.C: To stimulate a sleeping gland into producing maximum hormone levels
options.D: To permanently destroy overactive cells inside the adrenal cortex

explanation: Exactly! While stimulation tests wake glands up, suppression tests check if an overactive gland knows how to quiet down when it's supposed to. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is the HbA1c test so helpful for managing diabetes over time?

options.A: It detects acute kidney failure caused by high blood sugar spikes
options.B: It measures the exact amount of insulin stored inside pancreatic beta cells
options.C: It evaluates the immediate effect of the patient's last meal on glucose
options.D: It shows average blood sugar levels over the past two to three months

explanation: Spot on! Because sugar binds to red blood cells for their whole lifespan, HbA1c gives us a reliable historical report card of blood sugar over 2 to 3 months. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which imaging scan is usually best for getting a detailed look at the tiny pituitary gland?
explanation: You've got this! MRI gives amazing soft-tissue pictures, making it the top choice for checking out small, deep structures like the pituitary gland. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h5)

question: A patient is getting a CT scan with contrast dye for an adrenal tumor. What is a vital nursing check beforehand?

options.B: Checking for allergies to iodine or shellfish
options.C: Testing the patient for active thyroid antibodies
options.D: Ensuring the patient has swallowed radioactive iodine

explanation: Safety first! Contrast dye often contains iodine, so checking for allergies beforehand helps prevent severe allergic reactions. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h5)

question: What does a 'cold' nodule on a radioactive thyroid scan usually mean?

options.A: A hyperactive area that is producing excessive thyroid hormones
options.B: An allergic reaction to the contrast dye used during imaging
options.C: A normal section of tissue unaffected by the radioactive tracer
options.D: An area of low metabolic activity with a higher cancer risk

explanation: A 'cold' spot means the tissue didn't soak up the tracer well. That sluggish activity can sometimes point toward a higher risk of malignancy, requiring a closer look. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why must patients avoid iodine-heavy foods and meds before a radioactive iodine thyroid test?

options.A: Dietary iodine causes immediate allergic shock in all endocrine patients
options.B: Iodine completely destroys the scanning machine sensors during the test
options.C: Excess iodine can saturate the thyroid and interfere with tracer uptake
options.D: Non-radioactive iodine neutralizes the radiation inside the bloodstream

explanation: Think of the thyroid like a sponge. If it's already full of regular dietary iodine, it won't absorb the radioactive test tracer, messing up the results! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy on a thyroid lump?

options.A: To obtain cells for microscopic examination to check for cancer
options.B: To inject radioactive isotopes directly into the thyroid tissue
options.C: To completely remove the entire thyroid gland without surgery
options.D: To measure the 24-hour baseline hormone production levels

explanation: Spot on! An FNA takes a tiny sample of cells so the lab can check them under a microscope to confirm or rule out cancer. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the most crucial nursing check right after a neck biopsy or fine-needle aspiration?

options.A: Monitoring for signs of airway obstruction or bleeding
options.B: Checking for sudden spikes in fasting blood glucose
options.C: Testing the patient's 24-hour urine catecholamine levels

explanation: Always protect the airway! Since the procedure is right in the neck near major blood vessels and the trachea, nurses must watch closely for swelling or bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which nursing action is a must when managing a timed suppression test?

options.A: Stopping all patient monitoring once the initial baseline is drawn
options.B: Administering the suppression medication at random convenient times
options.C: Ensuring blood samples are drawn at the exact prescribed intervals
options.D: Allowing the patient to eat high-sugar meals during the test procedure

explanation: Precision is everything here! Dynamic tests rely completely on exact timing to track how hormone levels change after giving a medication. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h8)

question: A patient is very anxious about tests for a suspected adrenal tumor. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to refuse all invasive tests until they feel calmer
options.B: Provide clear, simple explanations of the tests and offer emotional support
options.C: Administer a strong sedative without a doctor's prescription
options.D: Reassure the patient that adrenal tumors are never cancerous

explanation: You're a natural! Clear, compassionate communication and emotional support go a long way in calming patient fears and helping them through tests. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h8)
